proof_checks.claim: First loss of simplicity is caught by a nonincident vertex-edge event
proof_checks.reason: After zero-length edges are excluded, a first nonadjacent transverse interior crossing is impossible because transverse crossings persist under small endpoint perturbations. Remaining contacts are endpoint-on-edge or collinear interval overlap, each containing a vertex-edge witness.

At the first adjacent overlap beyond the shared vertex, the shorter edge remote endpoint lies on the longer edge. Equal edge lengths give coincident remote endpoints. The remote endpoint is not a combinatorial endpoint of the opposite edge, matching the implementation nonincident enumeration.

proof_checks.claim: Area-zero events do not require an additional root family
proof_checks.reason: A polygonal Jordan curve encloses a nonempty open bounded interior of strictly positive area; a simple oriented ring has signed area equal to that area up to orientation. Area zero therefore entails edge collapse or loss of simplicity already covered.
T2a explicitly says post-contact degeneration causes whole-call out-of-domain, and out-of-domain is not no_contact or proof first contact does not exist.

proof_checks.claim: Audit zero has the requested post-contact-only implication
proof_checks.reason: The audit validates all 15220 step-block trajectories before any pair/broad-phase exclusion and finds zero invalid pairs among 64010. Post-contact-only rejections are a subset of all invalid pairs, so their count is rigorously zero without a separate prefix-contact solve.

audit_validation.interpretation_limit: This is production-contract recomputation on these stored trajectories, not an independent geometry oracle and not a universal claim that the conservative restriction never matters.
